title: Special comprehensive truth versus restricted name-dependent tastes
speaker: Qūnawī quoted, al-Mahāʾimī commenting
ontological_object: Names and particular divine presences relative to comprehensive perfection
governing_consideration: Distinguish primary attribution to one name from *jamʿ al-jamʿ* and most comprehensive perfection
mode_of_cognition: Spiritual taste evaluated for agreement with comprehensive knowledge
knower_station: Possessor of a particular *maqām* versus comprehensive realized knower
force_of_claim: Relative truth may be correct under one station while insufficient for an unrestricted claim
comparators: Turka SH-017 and Farghānī introductory distinction (navigation leads, not collated)
open_problem: Whether “what God knows” is here direct essential knowledge or its highest determinable disclosure

title: The limits of reporting complete realization
speaker: Qūnawī quoted, al-Mahāʾimī commenting
ontological_object: Absolute Essence as distinct from expressible relational assertions
governing_consideration: Distinguish expressibility in language from direct apprehension by a special state
mode_of_cognition: Theoretically inferable knowledge versus tasted shuhūd
force_of_claim: The claim that some attained knowledge cannot be written is epistemic, not a denial of divine intelligibility
open_problem: What is withheld because of intrinsic inexpressibility versus prudential concealment

title: The end of comprehensible perfection without encompassing the absolute
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī expounding cited prophetic prayers
ontological_object: Comprehensive divine perfection versus object comprehended by created cognition
governing_consideration: Knowledge can reach the perfection proper to a human knower without encompassing the Unrestricted
knower_station: Even the most accomplished human knower
force_of_claim: Station-conditioned limit; not numerical identity between finite and infinite knowledge
open_problem: Verify wording and attribution of earlier prophetic reports

title: Principial ordering of the first and second determinations
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī explanatory
ontological_object: First determination, second determination, intelligible intermediation
governing_consideration: Relations of unity and plurality vary at each principial level
knower_station: Knower able to distinguish levels of the divine names
force_of_claim: Ordered principial distinction, not alteration of God or temporal event
open_problem: Multiple traditional taxonomies do not map one-to-one by labels

title: Unrestricted necessary existence predicated under a determination
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī explicating Qūnawī
ontological_object: Real in pure negative unrestrictedness versus determinate intellective relation
governing_consideration: “One”, “necessary” and “unrestricted” themselves involve an *iʿtibār* at the relevant rank
knower_station: Qualified knower able to avoid equivocation
force_of_claim: Valid under a determinate cognitive relation; not automatically applied to the Absolute from every perspective
open_problem: What objective foundation has the first intelligible difference?

title: Mirrors and the difference between appearance and intrinsic alteration
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī elaborating Qūnawī
ontological_object: Intrinsic reality of reflected form and determinate modes of its appearance
governing_consideration: The mirror changes the aspect of manifestation, not the being of the Real in Himself
force_of_claim: Relationally grounded plurality; not a new property modifying the Unrestricted
comparators: Turka SH-030–031 coloured-glass analogy (verified existing handoff as lead)
open_problem: Whether any real effect at contingent level requires a distinct act of existing

title: Special essential disclosure as lightning-like
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī comments
ontological_object: Unrestricted Reality disclosed without a determinate locus
governing_consideration: Nonformal disclosure as distinct from ordinary name/attribute-specific theophanies
mode_of_cognition: Tasted shuhūd, not merely logical proof
force_of_claim: Duration characterised as no longer than a breath, relative to the report of such witnessing
open_problem: Whether literal temporal duration applies to every metaphysical register

title: The disappearance of bodily and psychical attention is not nonexistence
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Living human faculties at a station of nonattention
governing_consideration: Precisely «ليس معنى الفراغ ... عدمها في الواقع»
force_of_claim: Explicitly qualified cognitive claim; denial of ontological abolition
comparators: Ghazālī and Qushayrī citations pp.20–25; Qūnawī pp.108–110
open_problem: How do faculties persist under a nonformal disclosure that excludes attention to them?

title: Human comprehensiveness causes the flash not to endure
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī expounding Qūnawī
ontological_object: Human composite capacities and the brief special disclosure
governing_consideration: The recipient’s *jamʿiyya* simultaneously supports disclosure and requires the return of other functions
knower_station: Perfect Human, not a disembodied simple intellect
force_of_claim: Explanation of the experience’s transience; not of change in the divine Essence
comparators: Farghānī introductory human completeness (unverified text comparison); Turka
open_problem: Does the notion of a “breath” measure the disclosure or the recipient’s attention?

title: Statements “nothing with God” under an essential experience
speaker: Qūnawī cited; al-Mahāʾimī explains
ontological_object: Essence under disclosure versus eternal attributes and fixed relations
governing_consideration: Absence of separately witnessed things ≠ actual annihilation of attributes
mode_of_cognition: Tasted disclosure contrasted with rational conception
force_of_claim: Station-relative phrasing; neither attributes nor creatures cease to exist by mere change of attention
open_problem: Authenticated status of quoted sayings and their precise doctrinal scope

title: Fixed entities as unmade intelligible realities
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī constructs argument
ontological_object: Aʿyān in divine knowledge; manifested effects and divine act
governing_consideration: Distinguish uncreated intelligible reality from conditioned phenomenal showing
mode_of_cognition: Metaphysical argument joined to essential disclosure
knower_station: Knower of fixed entities under tasted unity
force_of_claim: Dependent interpretation, not a claim that worldly effects are self-subsistent
open_problem: What is the foundation of objective differentiation among unmade entities?

title: Relations condition multiplicity but mirrors do not produce it ex nihilo
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī interpreting Qūnawī
ontological_object: One existential self-disclosure and many receptive entities
governing_consideration: Manifest multiplicity comes through *nisba* to the mirrors, not their causal alteration of source
knower_station: Witness of the Real without a locus
force_of_claim: Valid under relational manifestation; no new intrinsic multiplicity of the Unrestricted
open_problem: Is the distinction objectively grounded without positing an extrinsic accident in God?

title: Rival causal descriptions as partially true
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī commenting
ontological_object: Attribution of agency to the Real, to forms and to their relations
governing_consideration: Different assignments of an effect may correspond to different valid aspects
knower_station: Knower in *baqāʾ* rather than exclusive effacement
force_of_claim: Explicit claim of **relative correctness** of competing attributions, not global equivalence
comparators: Turka SH-049–052; Thomist per se/participation (comparative only)
open_problem: Can both attributions preserve real created action without independent divinity?

title: As cause of plurality, the Real appears only in a viewed form
speaker: Qūnawī lemma, al-Mahāʾimī explains
ontological_object: Real as the intelligible source of plural forms
governing_consideration: Restriction *min ḥaythu huwa sabab li-l-kathra*: an aspect of causality, not the unrestricted Essence
knower_station: Knower of the cause in its determinate operation
force_of_claim: Aspect-qualified statement; not denial of disclosure without a locus in other respects
open_problem: Separate potential causal plenitude from actual displayed multiplicity

title: What a thing causes when considered without added conditions
speaker: Qūnawī lemma; al-Mahāʾimī comments
ontological_object: A source *qua itself* versus a configured causal whole
governing_consideration: The contrary does not issue under *min ḥaythu huwa huwa*, but may emerge with added conditions
mode_of_cognition: Rational causal analysis; hidden further aspect admitted as unmastered
technical_terms: min ḥaythu huwa huwa; shart; munāsaba
force_of_claim: Conditional universal rule; commentator’s conjecture is not claimed as unveiling
open_problem: Precise identity of the hidden additional consideration

title: Composite efficacy and the distinction between conditions and efficient links
speaker: Qūnawī quoted, al-Mahāʾimī explains
ontological_object: A complex of essential and extrinsic factors
governing_consideration: Effects are predicated of the contributing whole according to the governing rank
force_of_claim: No contradiction with intrinsic-source principle because its *iʿtibār* differs
open_problem: Determine scope of “each component has its effect” without contradicting p115

title: No identical second disclosure
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: One effusion, inexhaustible possibilities and recurrent manifestations
governing_consideration: Absolute repetition would leave no differentiating aspect of reality, rank or arrangement
force_of_claim: Not a rigorous physical law; denial of identity of manifestation under all respects
open_problem: Whether appeal to nonfinite possibilities is logically sound and how “twice” is measured

title: The first determination is not the negative Absolute
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī comments
ontological_object: Pure unrestrictedness and principial source of names
governing_consideration: Predicates require *taʿayyun*, and the many are ordered by a first determinate unity
force_of_claim: Principial priority, not temporal genesis
open_problem: Identify the first determination under each author independently

title: Two senses of predication in relation to names
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Divine names and their application to a qualified subject
governing_consideration: Separates *ḥaml al-muwāṭaʾa* from derivative attribution *ḥaml al-ishtiqāq*
mode_of_cognition: Logical analysis at a determinate stage
force_of_claim: Logical claim about names, not a direct ontology of multiple divine essences
open_problem: Which uses of predication are strictly linguistic versus ontic?

title: Essential and act-related attributes ordered without time
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī construing Qūnawī and citing kalām
ontological_object: Essential attributes and derivative act-related names
governing_consideration: Dependence in *dhāt*, not succession of events in *zamān*
force_of_claim: Relational priority, timeless on the commentator’s premises
comparators: Ashʿarī, Māturīdī, Avicenna (separate primary texts needed)
open_problem: Al-Mahāʾimī’s attributions of school positions need checking

title: Different gifts by predominance of the essential or nominal aspect
speaker: Qūnawī quoted and al-Mahāʾimī explains
ontological_object: Gifts to recipients under divine names
governing_consideration: Essential, nominal and mixed gifts classified by predominance of the relevant relation
knower_station: Recipient whose mode of asking conditions the gift
force_of_claim: Relational classification: no division of the absolute Essence into components
open_problem: What makes the predominance objective rather than merely classificatory?

title: Divine reckoning under names and nonnumerable essential gifts
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Gift, temporal conditions and eschatological answer
governing_consideration: Names have bounded domains whereas essential correspondences lack determinate numerical limit
force_of_claim: Some applications are eschatological and explicitly speculative
open_problem: What is asserted about punishment’s end versus relative transformation of its perception?

title: Priority of mercy over wrath as interpreted by al-Mahāʾimī
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī, attributing a position to Ibn ʿArabī
ontological_object: Ultimate divine mercy in the horizon of eschatology
governing_consideration: Priority of essential mercy over nominal punitive appearance
mode_of_cognition: Theological interpretation, not direct disclosed report here
knower_station: Saved and punished under different names
force_of_claim: Attributed doctrine, NOT settled universal Akbarian consensus
open_problem: Does the proposed eventual cessation of suffering mean objective end or altered receptivity?

title: Preparedness and existential condition as unspoken petition
speaker: Qūnawī quoted; al-Mahāʾimī classifies
ontological_object: Fixed entities, receptive capacities and natural conditions
governing_consideration: Distinct *suʾāl* according to *istiʿdād*, state, rank, spirit, temperament
mode_of_cognition: Ontology of receptivity and spiritual psychology
force_of_claim: No automatic equivalence of verbal request and ontological predisposition
open_problem: Does the Most Holy Effusion give possibility a determination or actual existence?

title: Condition does not mean cause
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī explicating Qūnawī
ontological_object: Intermediary ranked sources of effusion
governing_consideration: *Shart* depends-on without producing; *sabab* depends-on with efficacy
mode_of_cognition: Conceptual causal distinction and high-level witnessing
knower_station: Advanced recipients able to see Real in causes and conditions
force_of_claim: Formal/causal distinction within one comprehensive vision
comparators: Aquinas concurrence and Poinsot causality (comparative leads)
open_problem: Whether denying independence changes a condition into an efficient cause

title: One intelligible effusion determined by receptivities
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Primordial *fayḍ maʿnawī* and cosmic recipients
governing_consideration: No independent possibility-rule is attached to influx as it passes ranks
knower_station: Highest recipients under comprehension of source and result
force_of_claim: Relational determination without extrinsic modification of source
open_problem: How can objective differences have causes if the influx is intrinsically one?

title: Outward makes inward unity manifest as a plurality of forms
speaker: Qūnawī, explained by al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: al-Ẓāhir/al-Bāṭin, recipients, fixed entities and *shuʾūn*
governing_consideration: Inward unity includes possible plurality rather than opposing it; outward determinations reveal it
force_of_claim: Relative to divine name and disclosure, not total literal identity of objects
open_problem: Whether fixed entities are identical with name-rulings or grounded by them

title: Tasted unity cannot be exactly expressed as a subject and predicate
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī explaining Qūnawī
ontological_object: Nondual essential apprehension versus grammatical proposition
governing_consideration: Any assertion articulates subject/predicate or actor/acted-upon, introducing distinction
force_of_claim: Limit of expressibility for this realization, not abolition of all valid theology
open_problem: What makes a proposition valid when experiential nonduality escapes syntax?

title: Divine responsive accommodation is an admitted metaphor
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Response to prayer and human obedience
governing_consideration: Divine *muṭāwaʿa* is compared to an answer, not literal obedience
force_of_claim: Explicitly figurative; incompatible with divine subjection
open_problem: Is there a nonmetaphorical real relation corresponding to the figure?

title: Correct apprehension is not a mental image of the Essence
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Divine Presence witnessed in things under names
governing_consideration: Affirm seeing the Real in all things without *ḥulūl*, *ittiḥād*, or confinement
mode_of_cognition: Discursive knowledge and disclosed witnessing distinguished
force_of_claim: Positive qualified conception, not sensory form
open_problem: What differentiates apprehension of a name from projecting a fantasy?

title: Mental imagery and the risk of praying to one’s own conception
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Represented divine figure versus Real under true names
governing_consideration: False identification of finite mental construction as the unrestricted Real
mode_of_cognition: Inference from scriptural address and epistemic introspection
force_of_claim: Conditional claim about **specific answer**, not absolute refusal of all supplication
open_problem: Does the argument require an implausibly perfect concept for all answered prayer?

title: Divine accompaniment distinguished from absolute identity
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: One divine Reality and all created images
governing_consideration: *Maʿiyya* under names is not Essence physically inhabiting a representation
force_of_claim: Qualified presence, not indwelling or equality of God and mental objects
open_problem: How is divine universal withness compatible with distinct actuality?

title: Correct but partial name-bound knowledge at intermediate station
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Particular divine name/attribute as known and invoked
governing_consideration: Valid under some divine ranks, not comprehensive of all names
mode_of_cognition: Correct conception and shuhūd, but partial
knower_station: Intermediate among the people of God
force_of_claim: Station-conditioned adequacy; not simply false because less comprehensive
open_problem: What are necessary and sufficient conditions for calling a bounded perspective “correct”?

title: Flash ceases but its complete apprehension persists
speaker: Qūnawī with explicit commentary of al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Essential disclosure versus the abiding human cognitive state
governing_consideration: A single brief essential disclosure yields enduring *maʿrifa* comprehending all names and ranks
mode_of_cognition: Direct essential witnessing followed by synthesis
force_of_claim: Explicit phenomenological temporal distinction: *tajallī* ends; cognition remains
comparators: Compare Mashraʿ pp108–110 with pp136–137, Fanārī *Miṣbāḥ* (lead)
open_problem: Does the continued representation persist by habitual *malaka*, as form, or by ongoing support?

title: Knowledge of decree conditions perfect petition
speaker: Qūnawī and al-Mahāʾimī
ontological_object: Divine knowledge, tablet and Pen, manifested events
governing_consideration: Distinguish intrinsically impossible from what is impossible *given prior divine knowledge*
mode_of_cognition: Disclosure across ranks, not inference from observed past
technical_terms: lawḥ maḥfūẓ; maqām qalamī; mustaḥīl bi-l-ʿilm
force_of_claim: Claims of realized apprehension of decree; no inference that all humans know destiny
comparators: Avicenna on divine knowledge, Ṭūsī and later kalām (not collated)
open_problem: Does a conditional decree threaten freedom, and what is the source of its counterfactual contingency?

title: Definitive versus suspended decree and unspoken volition
speaker: Al-Mahāʾimī explaining Qūnawī
ontological_object: Cosmic events as unconditioned or conditioned by an appointed means
governing_consideration: *Jāzim* decree versus *muʿallaq* decree requiring petition, willing or other causes
knower_station: Knower whose aspiration is aligned with decree
force_of_claim: A cause under decree, not self-subsisting creaturely existentiation
open_problem: Exact distinction between knowledge of an event and determination of its occurrence
